questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A European destination with many other Erasmus students.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was fine, the UNIMI Erasmus office answers quite quickly when asked questions

questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used SpotAHome which was fine. The booking charge is a little expensive but real estate sites like Idealista have LOADS of scams so I would use spotahome or a similar site to be sure. UNIMI has a discount code for the SpotAHome booking charge you can find it on the website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You can live in some better parts of the city when you live off campus but it will cost you much more. 

The dorms are super cheap, like 300 EUR per month but they are FAR from the center and you live with another person in your room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is very different from UCPH. You can shop around for different courses in the first few weeks. There is no real deadline for signing up for a course only for signing up for the exams. Some courses do have attendance though (most of the courses of the social sciences campus) but the professors are rarely strict about it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fully successful. I was also able to take a math course "Stochastic Control Optimisation" which is in Italian but the professor let me self-study it and take the exam in English

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If there is an Italian course you *really* want to take, ask the professor. Sometimes they will let you self-study it, or sometimes they will even be fine with lecturing in English

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The English courses were bad, low level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The Italian math course I took was hard, everything else quite easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No exercise classes or problem sheets

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Local culture is very nice (not the academic part). Italians are very social.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians can be a bit cavalier about schedules and time

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperitivo. Going out and eating out is very cheap. Cafes

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate in some of the Erasmus organisation stuff in the beginning you will meet many nice people and also a lot of non-Danes
Exams are very strange especially oral. All student taking the course sit in the same room and see the exam/grade.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gold bao in Chinatown is amazing

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met a lot of great people and I opened up more.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and girlfriend
